candidates.name: tod_fade_since_open_1005_1030
candidates.description: Between 10:05 and 10:29 (signal on the close of each 1-min bar with 65 <= mod < 90), the rule compares the bar close with today's 09:00 opening price. If price is above the day open it sells, and if below it buys, fading the move made since the open. Entry is at the next bar's open, one position at a time, with re-entry allowed while still inside the window. Bracket is target 500 / stop 500, with forced exit at end of day. There are no other filters.
candidates.rationale: In 2012 only futures traded from 09:00 to 10:00. The cash-equity market opened at 10:00 BRT and the US cash market at 10:30 BRT, and volume per 30-min bucket confirms this (6.7k, 8.5k, 12.1k, 19.6k). The idea is that the thin futures-only move overshoots, then partially reverts once cash liquidity and index arbitrage arrive (after the opening auction prints settle, around 10:05), until the US open brings a new shock. Fading at exactly 10:00-10:04 does NOT work (t about -0.5), which fits the story that the futures keep moving while the cash index catches up at its open. Robustness inside discovery: profitable for window starts 55-70 and ends 85-100 and for every target >= 300 with stop 400-500. TS neighbours: 400/500 t 2.15, 500/400 t 2.86, 400/400 t 2.09, 300/500 t 2.80. Positive in May, June and July, 10 of 13 weeks positive, long and short both positive (+5781 / +8010). Bootstrap 90% CI of daily mean is [111, 353] pts. Free parameters: start minute, end minute (fixed at the US open by rationale) and the bracket. CAVEATS: this was found after a screen of about 2,300 variants. Earlier screens pointed to morning reversal, and the window, the 09:00-open anchor and the 10:05 start were all refined on this same data. Other anchors were weaker (previous close, 09:15, 09:30, 09:45, 10:00 gave t 1.6-2.1 at zero cost). A placebo scan of the same fade at all 90 five-minute slots shows |t| about 3 clusters elsewhere, with opposite sign at 12:05-12:20, so the sample noise is large. Rough family-wise chance of a result this strong appearing by luck is about 10-15%. Expect heavy shrinkage out of sample. The clock times depend on the 2012 B3/US session schedule (US DST, no Brazilian DST); validation and holdout fall in the same regime.

candidates.name: tod_fade_since_open_single_1010
candidates.description: Once per day, on the close of the first bar at or after 10:09 (mod >= 69 and < 90), the rule compares the close with today's 09:00 opening price. If price is above the open it sells, and if below it buys. Entry is at the next bar's open (about 10:10), bracket target 500 / stop 500, forced exit at end of day, one trade per day. This is the same hypothesis as time_of_day_1 in its simplest single-entry form.
candidates.rationale: Same effect as time_of_day_1. It must NOT be counted as independent confirmation: if one fails out of sample, treat both as failed. It is simpler, with one timing parameter plus the bracket. Sign-randomization at the same entry bars gives p = 0.00045. Going all-long or all-short at those same bars loses (-1256 / -1268), so the edge is in the direction choice, not in timing alone. Positive in all 3 months, 11 of 13 weeks positive, longs +6163 and shorts +5746. Signal-minute neighbours at 500/500: 10:07 t 2.9, 10:11 t 2.1, 10:14 t 1.5, 10:17 t 2.4, 10:20 t 2.0, all profitable. 10:04 is t 0.9 and 10:00 is negative, so the edge is absent right at the cash open. TS neighbours: 400/500 t 3.1, 500/400 t 3.25, 400/400 t 2.96, 300/500 t 2.59. 10:10 sits near the peak of the signal-minute scan, so the in-sample t of 3.35 is optimistic. The same multiple-testing caveats apply: about 2,300 variants evaluated, and the effect was located with data-driven screens.

observations:
Overall: one effect survived (fading the move since the 09:00 open, between about 10:05 and 10:30), submitted in two correlated formulations. Treat it as ONE hypothesis with modest prior credibility: it was found after about 2,300 evaluated variants (descriptive screens included), and its discovery t of about 3.1-3.4 corresponds to roughly a 10-15% family-wise chance of being luck. Everything else in the time-of-day lens failed.

WHAT DID NOT WORK:
(1) Pure seasonality by 30-min bucket. Mean returns per bucket: 2 of 17 at |t| about 2 (12:30 -127, 13:30 +79), which is what chance predicts. 500/500 bracket expectancy is negative in every bucket for both directions, the best being about +45/trade (t 0.8). Also, random_baseline is matched on bucket and direction, so a pure clock-drift rule cannot pass criterion 3 by construction. A time-of-day rule must contain day-selection information.
(2) Day of week. Open-to-close and bracket expectancy show nothing (|t| < 1.5, about 12 days per weekday).
(3) Intraday momentum (Gao et al.: first half-hour or move-to-16:30 predicting the last half-hour). Absent, t 0.2-0.7.
(4) First-bar, first-5, first-15 and first-30-minute direction. Immediate trades in either direction lose. Right after the first 3-5 minutes there is short-term continuation: fade trades at k=2-4 have t -2 to -4.8, while follow trades are about 0 to +2 and patchy. The first-5-min direction does predict the opposite drift to the close (zero-cost t 2.5-3.3, both halves). This is NOT tradeable with brackets of 500 or less: single bracket trades are noise and change sign with entry time, and re-entering all day bleeds from costs (best t 1.7).
(5) Gap. It partially fades in the first 5-15 min (corr -0.31/-0.35) but continues later. Gap-fade at the open and gap-follow at 09:05-09:30 both have t < 1.8. Gap-pullback (gap direction after an early counter-move) at 09:30 reaches t 1.9 but with n 36.
(6) US macro release minutes (09:30 and 11:00 BRT). The first 1-3 minutes' move tends to revert over 30 min (corr -0.2 to -0.34), but these minutes rank only about 5th-50th of 479 when every minute is scanned, so this is indistinguishable from noise.
(7) The 10:30 US open is the highest volume and range bucket but has no predictable direction: mild momentum (t up to 1.7), no reversal of the 10:00-10:30 pre-open move.
(8) Lunch and midday. Consecutive 30/60-min windows from 11:30 to 14:30 show mild positive autocorrelation, all 10 correlations positive but individually t < 2.2. Following the move since the open at 12:05-12:20 looked strong as a mirror image (the fade loses with t -2.8 to -3.9), but the follow version after costs is patchy across minutes (t -2.2 to +2.6) and window versions reach t < 1.3. Rejected.
(9) Costs dominate small brackets. The round trip is about 25 pts (stop trades pay exit slippage plus fee; target trades pay only the fee but need 1 tick through), which is about 12% of a 200 bracket. Every high-frequency re-entry rule with 200-300 brackets died. Wider stops (500) were consistently better.
(10) Placebo warning. The same fade-since-open rule scanned at 90 five-minute slots gives t from -3.9 to +3.4 (sd 1.25), with clusters at both ends. |t| of about 3 is not rare in 59 days of this data. The 10:05-10:25 cluster is the only positive one that also has a microstructure story and survives costs. Even so, the 10:00 hole and the dependence on the 09:00-open anchor (other anchors give t 1.6-2.1) mean it was partly shaped by the data.

Market facts learned: average daily range about 3,430 pts (500 pts is about 15% of it). The discovery period trended down (mean open-to-close -308/day). Volume ramps at 10:00 (cash open) and peaks at 10:30 (US open). Morning, 09:30-11:00: negative autocorrelation (reversal of the futures-only move). Midday: mild momentum. Afternoon: noisy sign flips. Validation and holdout (26 Jul to Sep 2012) fall in the same session-hours regime, so the clock-based rule stays meaningful there. It would need re-mapping for periods with different B3/US hours. Out-of-sample expectations, if real: the effect probably shrinks well below the in-sample +125 to +200 pts/trade. With only 20 validation days (about 20-37 trades), the out-of-sample test has low power, so a pass should not be over-read either.
best_near_misses: Not submitted. (a) Gap-pullback at 09:30: trade in the gap direction if the first 30 minutes moved against it. Best t 1.9 at 500/300, n 36 (< 40). (b) Fade the first-30-min move at 09:30, one trade per day: t 1.7 at 300/300, while the k=14 and k=19 neighbours are negative. (c) Fade the move since the open with re-entries from 12:00 to close: t up to 1.7 at 400/500 and 500/500, all other cells worse. (d) Follow the move since the open at 12:20, single trade: t 2.1-2.6 at several brackets, but adjacent minutes 12:00 and 12:25 are negative or about 0 and window versions are t < 1.3, so it is not a plateau. (e) Fade the move of the last 60 minutes, re-entering during 10:00-10:30: t 2.7 at 400/500 (p 0.003), but it fails at lookback 45 (t 0.3), so it was superseded by the cleaner since-open anchor. (f) A single fade of the first hour at exactly 10:00 LOSES at every bracket (t -2.1 to -0.2), even though it is the most natural form of the hypothesis. This is the strongest argument against the submitted candidates and was reported, not hidden.

candidates.name: OR30 first-break fade before cash open
candidates.description: The opening range is the high/low of bars 09:00-09:29. From 09:30, find the FIRST 1-min bar of the day that closes outside that range. If that bar is at or before 09:59 (before the Bovespa cash-equity open at 10:00), trade against the break at the next bar's open: a close above the high means sell, a close below the low means buy. At most one trade per day; no trade if the first break comes at 10:00 or later. Bracket +500/-500, otherwise exit at end of day.
candidates.rationale: Before 10:00 the future trades thin, with no cash-equity flow (volume jumps about 1.6x at 10:00 in the data), so the first escape from the early range tends to be a fake-out that reverts. Checks that support it: momentum on the same event loses heavily (mirror image). The effect is positive across OR lengths 15-35 min and in all 16 target/stop combos for OR 15/20/30. It decays smoothly as the OR gets longer (OR 40-60 is flat or negative). Placebo ranges built after 10:00 (10:00-10:15, 10:00-10:30, 11:00-11:30, 12:00-12:30) show NO fade edge, and momentum on them also loses. Breaks after 10:00 are about break-even. The edge survives entry delays of 1-5 bars (500/500), so it is not a one-bar bounce. Long and short sides both contribute (22 trades each). Positive in each third of the period (+2808/+2392/+3354). Positive in all OR-width terciles. Day-bootstrap P(total<=0)=0.003. CAVEATS: only 44 events (31 wins, 13 losses). The 10:00 cutoff was chosen after seeing that post-10:00 breaks did not work: it is structural (cash open), but it is a 3rd free choice besides OR length and the symmetric bracket. A sign-flip permutation over 256 configs of this one family gives family-wise p about 0.02-0.07; across the whole 2657-variant search it is probably about 0.1 or worse. It was found in one high-volatility regime (Euro crisis, discovery ends the day before the Draghi speech). In-sample avg/trade (+194) is surely inflated by selection; a realistic expectation, if real, is much lower. Neighbors at N=25/35 and T/S 400-500 are all profitable (t 1.75-2.91).

candidates.name: OR30 first-break fade (any time)
candidates.description: The opening range is the high/low of bars 09:00-09:29. From 09:30, the FIRST 1-min bar of the day that closes outside the range triggers a trade against the break at the next bar's open (close above the high: sell; close below the low: buy), whatever time it happens (the library blocks entries after 17:00). Exactly one signal per day. Bracket +500/-500, otherwise exit at end of day.
candidates.rationale: SAME HYPOTHESIS as breakout_vol_1 without the 10:00 cutoff, so strictly 3 free parameters (OR length, target, stop). 44 of its 59 trades are identical to breakout_vol_1; the 15 extra post-10:00 trades were roughly break-even in discovery. Validators should treat _1 and _2 as ONE hypothesis, not two independent confirmations. Neighbors: N=20/25 t 2.09/2.39 and N=35 t 1.25 at 500/500; 400/500 t 2.41 and 500/400 t 1.81 at N=30; all positive. Same caveats as _1 (59 events, one regime, multiple testing).

observations:
Cost reality: random entries lose about -31 pts/trade at every bracket size (gross is about 0 at zero cost). Breakeven win rate at 500/500 base is about 51.3% (wins pay about +494, losses about -519 because the stop wins ties and the target must trade 1 tick through). Almost every high-frequency breakout rule in this lens just pays costs.

WHAT DID NOT WORK (all on discovery data, all 16 target/stop combos, base costs):
(1) Classic ORB momentum (OR 5/15/30/60/90 min, first-only or every break): uniformly negative, about -45 pts/trade, worse than random. Momentum after the first OR break is strongly negative (t down to -2.8).
(2) New intraday highs/lows after 9:30/10:00/11:00, by close or by touch, momentum or fade: all negative. Late-day (after 14:30/15:30) first new HOD/LOD, either way: noise.
(3) Rolling Donchian 15/30/60-bar breakouts, with or without a squeeze filter (channel width vs a 120-bar ATR): all negative; momentum on 15-bar breaks was the worst (t -3.2).
(4) ATR-scaled shock bars (range > 2-4x ATR60, close at the extreme) and 5/15-bar moves > 2-3 ATR*sqrt(m), either way: random or negative.
(5) Failed ORB with confirmation (break, then close back inside, optional 15-bar limit): about random or negative. The fade only works if entered right after the first break, not after waiting for re-entry.
(6) Turtle-soup failed breaks of 30/60/120-bar extremes: strongly negative (pays costs on hundreds of trades).
(7) Prior-day high/low first cross, either way: noise.
(8) 5-min NR4/NR7 bar breakouts, either way: negative.
(9) 30-bar breakouts on volume spikes (2-3x): negative.
(10) Bollinger squeeze (std20/std-avg < 0.6/0.8) then a 2-sd band break: negative.
(11) Generic early fades: fading the return since the open at fixed times 9:20/9:30/9:45/9:59 was about random, and fading the first 0.15/0.25/0.35% excursion from the open was weak (best t 1.2). So the established-range break matters, not just distance from the open. This is mildly worrying for the mechanism.
(12) First-break of ranges built after the cash open (10:00-10:15, 10:00-10:30, 10:30-11:00, 11:00-11:30, 12:00-12:30, 14:00-14:30), momentum or fade: no edge. Fade of 10:00-10:30 and 11:00-11:30 ranges was negative in all 16 combos.

WHAT WORKED: only one effect. Fading the FIRST close outside an early opening range (OR 15-30 min), one trade per day, is positive in 15-16 of 16 target/stop combos for OR 15/20/25/30. It concentrates in breaks before the 10:00 cash-equity open (avg about +200/trade for breaks at 9:30-10:00, negative for breaks after 10:00). Tight 200 stops are much weaker (whipsaw). Stops of 300-500 work. Weaknesses: OR15/20/25 versions were about flat in the first third of the period. Cross-half selection: choosing the best config on H1 gave mean t 2.09 in H2, but choosing on H2 gave only t 0.68 in H1. OR30 was the only length consistent across thirds. Family-wise sign-flip permutation over 256 configs of this family: P(max t >= 3.42) = 0.02 and P(>= 2.71) = 0.07. Counting the whole 2657-variant search, the honest family-wise significance is probably about 0.1 or worse.

Context: May-Jul 2012 was a high-volatility Euro-crisis bear phase (avg daily range about 3430 pts, avg day -307 pts). The locked periods (Aug-Sep 2012, after the Draghi speech) are likely a calmer, rallying regime, so the effect could easily fail to transfer. With about 15-20 trades per 20-day OOS window, even a real edge of +50-100/trade would be hard to confirm statistically. Treat both candidates as ONE weak-to-moderate hypothesis, not a validated edge.
best_near_misses: Same family: OR15 first-break fade with the 10:00 cutoff at 300/300 (n=56, t 2.82, p<0.001, stress +3579, but first third about flat). OR25 with cutoff at 500/500 (n=48, t 2.91, first third weak +783). OR20 any-time, close trigger, 500/500 (t 2.09). Touch-trigger versions of OR15/20 first-break fade (t up to 3.52 at 300/400 for OR15 touch) were not chosen because they are less conservative and highly correlated. The asymmetric 200-300 target / 400-500 stop versions have the highest t (up to 3.4) but carry tail risk out of sample (one loss wipes out 2-3 wins). Original ORB fade on both sides (first up-break and first down-break each day): OR15/30 at 200/500 had t 2.2, but the second (opposite-side) break of the day loses, so it is inferior to first-break-only. Outside this family nothing came close: the best other result was 15-bar 3-ATR move fade, with t 1.87 on only 14 trades.

observations:
RESULT: no candidate. Nothing in this lens meets the discovery bar in a stable way, so I wrote nothing to candidates/. Everything used only load() (the discovery period). Scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-codex-teste/6018d537-360c-53a0-852b-fd7bc8336aa9/scratchpad/edge/logs/meanrev_momentum/. My fast backtester matches wf.backtest exactly. Variant count: 7,980 backtested combinations (rule x params x fade/follow x 16 target/stop pairs) plus about 240 zero-cost exploratory slices, logged as 8,220.

1) Structure before costs (forward returns from the next bar's open, t-stats clustered by day):
- Short-term reversal at 1-5 minutes is real but tiny: about -5 pts of 5-min forward return per sigma of the 5-min move (t about -2.5). Round-trip cost is about 25-32 pts and the target is at least 200 pts, so it can't be traded.
- 30-60 min moves have no linear predictive power.
- 120-min momentum is weak (about +69 pts per z over the next 60 min, t 2.25), and nearly all of it is in the first half (the May selloff). In the second half t is about 0.5.
- VWAP deviation, position in the day's range, distance from the 60-bar mean and distance from the day's open have no linear power (|t| < 1.2 at every horizon).
- Overnight gap: price tends to move AGAINST the gap in the first 5-20 minutes, by about 100-130 pts on average (t -2.7 at 5 min). It is concentrated in the first half and is too small for a 200+ pt target after costs. The path then drifts back in the gap direction (not significant).
- Day level: the known 'first half-hour predicts last half-hour' effect is absent (t 0.1). The first hour does NOT continue afterwards; if anything it reverses slightly (t -0.85). Prior-day return: fading it is weakly positive and following it is negative, neither robust.

2) Rule families tested at base costs (the mean t across a family is a useful health check):
- Fade/follow crossings of z-scored k-min moves (k = 1, 3, 5, 10, 15, 30, 60, 120; thresholds 2-3.5), distance from the 60-bar mean, VWAP z and distance from the open (1,472 variants): 0 passed, best t 1.05. Family mean t is negative for both fade and follow. Fading streaks of 4-7 consecutive closes is worst (mean t -2.1).
- After shocks, tight 200-pt stops are destroyed by the volatility that follows the spike. Only 500-pt stops come close to breakeven.
- Pullback within a trend (context from distance to open or VWAP, plus a 5- or 15-min pullback), all gap rules at 9:00, 9:15 and 9:30, VWAP crosses, first-hour continuation (single and repeated entries), late-day momentum, VWAP rules by time window, distance from prior close in daily-sigma units, volatility-regime filters, volume-conditioned moves (the Llorente-style idea that high-volume moves continue and low-volume moves reverse), long-only and short-only splits, opening-window fades, and gap fade with re-entry: all failed.
- The only variants passing the first screen (about 15 of 8,000) were isolated spikes, as expected by chance.

3) Multiple-testing calibration:
- Placebo: the same 736-rule structure with random event directions produced 0-2 'passes' per 736 variants (max t 1.2-2.4). At my scale, about 5-10 lucky passes would be expected. I got about 15 and none survived the neighbour check.
- The best t over all variants with n >= 40 is 2.55. That is far below the roughly 3.4-4.2 expected as the best of thousands of partly correlated variants. There is no evidence of an edge in mean reversion or momentum at a 200-500 pt target/stop after realistic costs in this sample.

4) Caveats:
- The discovery period is short (59 days) and has a strong regime split: a May selloff of about -15%, then a range and recovery. Many 'momentum' results come only from May.
- Rules with one trade per day (gap, news time, first hour) are capped at about 58 trades, so they can almost never reach t >= 2 honestly.
best_near_misses:
All of these look attractive on their own (random-entry p 0.0005-0.005, still positive under stress costs, both halves positive) but fail the neighbour-stability rule (criterion 5) and/or t >= 2. Do NOT trade them; they show what overfitting looks like here.
(a) After 15:00, follow price crossing +/-0.75 VWAP-z away from VWAP; target 200 / stop 400: n 58, total +4491, t 2.55, halves +2938 / +1553, stress +4233, p 0.0005. A fine threshold scan shows a narrow spike: thresholds 0.75-0.8 are good, 0.6 and 0.9 are about zero, and 0.5 and 1.0 are clearly negative (t -1 to -2.6). REJECTED.
(b) Fade the 3-minute reaction to the 9:30 US-data minute (signal at 9:32); target 400 / stop 500: n 57, total +6921, t 2.17, halves +5025 / +1896, stress +6332, p 0.0045. A 1-minute window gives t about -0.9 and a 5-minute window about 0, so it is isolated. It also relies on time-of-day mappings that move when daylight saving changes. REJECTED.
(c) In the first 40 minutes, fade a 3-minute move above 2 sigma; target 500 / stop 400: n 81, total +8952, t 2.10, halves +6770 / +2182, stress +6148, p 0.001. Neighbouring thresholds 1.5 and 2.5 and the 5-minute version are all near zero. It is a corner spike. REJECTED.
(d) Gap fade at 9:01; target 400 / stop 300: n 58, total +5013, t 1.85, p 0.002, stress +4327. This has the best economic story (the gap tends to start filling in the first 5-20 minutes) but it is below t 2, mostly from the first half, and has at most about 58 trades. It may be worth monitoring, but there is no edge proven.

candidates.name: volume_flow_0930_volswitch
candidates.description: Runs once per day, at the close of the 09:30 one-minute bar. That is the minute of the US 08:30 ET macro releases (09:30 Brasilia while US daylight time is on). It takes the session move (close of the 09:30 bar minus the open of the session's first bar) and the cumulative contracts traded (qty) from the open through 09:30. That volume is compared with the median of the same 09:30 cumulative volume over the previous 10 sessions (at least 3 needed). If volume is at or above the median, it follows the morning move (buy if up, sell if down). If volume is below the median, it fades the move. Entry is at the 09:31 open, with a 500 target and a 500 stop; any open position is closed at the end of the day. At most one trade per day.
candidates.rationale: HIGH OVERFIT RISK. Treat this as a hypothesis for the locked out-of-sample (OOS) test, not as an edge. The story is Campbell-Grossman-Wang / Llorente et al.: low-volume moves revert and high-volume, information-driven moves continue, with the US-data minute as the information event. That story was written AFTER the result, which came from scanning decision times T in {10,15,20,25,30,35,40,45,60,90} min after 09:00. It passes every discovery check as written. In a selection-aware null (shuffling the volume labels, or random direction per day, max t over the same 160 combinations of time and target/stop) none of 300 null draws reached the observed max t (p<0.0033 inside that family). The 10/20-day lookbacks also work, as do thresholds 1.1/1.2 and decision time T=31, and all 16 target/stop pairs are positive at T=30/31. Each month is positive (May +5327, June +1771, July +1823). Bootstrap of the mean per trade: 5th percentile +52 pts. Points AGAINST: (1) It is a spike in time. T=20/25/29 give nothing or lose. T=30 averages +6235 pts over the 16 target/stop pairs, against +4088 at T=31, +2108 at T=32 and under +800 at T=33/34. (2) The same switch logic FAILS at every other test I ran: 10:00 cash open, 10:30 US open, 11:00 (the 10:00 ET releases), the 09:00 opening gap, and 09:10-09:25. (3) It is fragile. Threshold 0.8/0.9 gives weak results, and measuring direction with VWAP distance instead of the session move kills it. Using the 09:30 bar's own volume and direction (the purest news measure) gives a negative result. (4) Direction differs from T=29 on only about 8 of 55 days, and the 9 trades with a morning move under 10 ticks (direction nearly arbitrary) all won. (5) Only 55 trades, one per day, after about 1270 variants. My estimate that it is real: about 20%. Do not trade it unless it clearly survives validation AND holdout. Other target/stop pairs looked better in sample (400/400 t=3.84, 300/400 t=3.86). I chose 500/500 because it is the user's stated maximum and the least data-selected pair.

observations: Overall: on 1-minute OHLCV, volume and flow proxies carry almost no usable directional information for 200-500 pt brackets once costs are paid. Base costs are about 32 pts per round trip (about 2.5 ticks). Rank correlations of every volume/flow feature with returns 5-60 min ahead were |rho| <= 0.04 when sampled honestly (relative volume vs time-of-day norm, average trade size qty/trades, close-location value (CLV), volume-weighted CLV pressure over 5-60 bars, tick-rule signed volume, VWAP distance). The best gross conditional edges were about 20-60 pts per trade with t around 1-2 and halves that disagree. Tested and FAILED: (a) Volume-climax bars (relative volume >= 2.5-5x the time-of-day norm), fade or follow by bar, 5-bar or 15-bar direction: about 0 gross. (b) Large average trade size ('institutional') bars, follow or fade: about 0. (c) Absorption (high volume, small range), fade the prior move or follow CLV: noise. (d) 60-bar breakouts on low vs high volume: low-volume breakouts did slightly better (+49 gross, t 1.2), the opposite of folklore, but not significant. (e) Big 15-bar moves on low volume faded / high volume followed: about 0. (f) Price-vs-pressure divergence over 15/30/60 bars: following the pressure LOST (div30 -65 gross, t -2.0, a likely fluke among many tests). (g) Volume regime direction ('quiet = long, loud = short'): looks good on raw forward returns only because the sample trends down and high volume comes with selloffs. Against same-direction random entries it adds about 20-50 gross: not enough. (h) Selling/buying climax at new intraday extremes with a wick: nothing (the strictest version -85 gross). (i) Prior-day volume point of control (POC) or prior-day VWAP touches: the VWAP break-follow had +84 gross (t 1.9, both halves positive) but was negative after costs for 14 of 16 target/stop pairs. (j) Cumulative volume-weighted CLV since the open shows mean reversion in the first 45 min and late in the day (rho -0.2 to -0.3 on a 59-day once-a-day sample). The trading versions failed: one fade per day at 09:30/09:45/10:00 reached t <= 1.82, and a fade every 30 or 60 min reached t <= 1.13 with unstable halves. (k) Late-day flow into the close: nothing significant. (l) Opening gap with an opening-volume switch: negative. Structural facts: the 09:30 bar is the US 08:30 ET release minute. Its mean volume is 2.4x that of nearby bars and about 5x on Thursdays (jobless claims). Its range is about 1.5x normal. The only rule in my lens that passed the bar is tied to that minute and is fragile (see candidate caveats). The discovery period has a strong down-drift (real price about 63k to 52k), so any rule that leans short on high-volume or volatile states looks better than it is. Always compare against same-direction random entries. Variant count logged: 1273 (1101 backtest/event-study configurations plus about 172 exploratory screen cells), via log_variants('volume_flow', 1273). Scratch scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-codex-teste/6018d537-360c-53a0-852b-fd7bc8336aa9/scratchpad/edge/logs/volume_flow/.
best_near_misses: 1) Morning fade of the session's cumulative pressure: at 09:45, one trade per day against the sign of the volume-weighted CLV since the open. 12 of 16 target/stop pairs positive, best t_daily 1.77 (300/400), 500/500 t=1.25, both halves positive. It is a price-reversal effect (fading the raw session move does almost as well) and below the bar. 2) Prior-day VWAP touch, follow the break: +84 pts gross per trade at 500/500 with zero costs (t 1.9, both halves positive), but after base costs it is about +13 per trade (t 0.24) and negative for most target/stop pairs. 3) Late-day relative volume (30-bar mean of relative volume at 16:49) vs the return into the close: rho +0.24 (halves +0.21/+0.29) on 59 days. Not traded, borderline, and the 40-minute window rarely reaches 500 pts. None of these should be traded.

candidates.name: levels_calendar_1_pdc_conditional_10h_range_break
candidates.description: The reference levels are yesterday's last close (PDC) and the 09:00-09:59 range, which is the futures-only hour before the 10:00 cash-equity open. From 10:00 on, the rule takes the FIRST bar that closes at or above the 9h range high (with the previous close below it) and the FIRST bar that closes at or below the 9h range low (with the previous close above it). That gives at most one up-break and one down-break per day. At that bar it checks whether price has traded at PDC at any point since today's open. If yes (the gap is filled, so the day is two-sided), it FADES the break: short an up-break, buy a down-break. If no (the gap is still open, so the day is one-sided), it FOLLOWS the break. Entry is at the next bar's open, with target 300 and stop 500 adjusted points. Library rules apply: one position at a time, no entries after 17:00, flat at the last bar. There are 3 free parameters: range length of 60 minutes, target and stop.
candidates.rationale: Rationale: in 2012 WIN traded from 09:00 but cash equities opened at 10:00, so the 9h range is the overnight and foreign repositioning range. A return to PDC means the overnight imbalance has been absorbed (a balanced day), so range edges hold and breaks fail. If PDC was never touched, initiative traders are in control and breaks extend. Evidence: all 16 target/stop cells are positive. Neighbors: 300/400 t2.82, 400/500 t2.63, 500/500 t2.48, 200/500 t2.13, 400/400 t2.17, 200/400 t1.96. Both arms are positive (fade arm 37 trades +5989, follow arm 49 trades +3823), and longs and shorts are both positive (+5312 / +4500). Shuffling the filled/unfilled labels gives p=0.003. Shifting the PDC reference by +/-0.3% weakens the result and +/-0.6% removes it; using the prior-day midpoint or prior-day open as the filter shows nothing. The result holds up to strict-vs-inclusive break definitions, 1-2 tick margins, a static gap-filled flag fixed at 10:00 (t 2.7) and signal cutoffs at 13h/15h (t 3.3-3.5). CAVEATS, important: (1) It was found after 5225 variants, and a t of about 3 is roughly what the best of many correlated variants can produce by chance. (2) M=60 is a local peak: M=55/65 give t of about 1-1.7, and M=45 or 30 give nothing or negative. The cash open justifies 60, but the peak is probably inflated. (3) Performance by 10-day block was +2711, +2485, +1447, +3073, +861, -765. The edge faded over the last ~19 days as volatility fell. (4) It relies on a wide stop and small target (78% win rate, asymmetric payoff); S=300 or S=200 are only marginal. Expect heavy shrinkage out of sample; zero is a realistic outcome.

candidates.name: levels_calendar_2_pdc_conditional_stale_extreme_break
candidates.description: The reference levels are yesterday's last close (PDC) and today's running high and low. A signal fires when a bar CLOSES above the day's high so far and that high had stood for at least 30 bars, or CLOSES below the day's low so far and that low had stood for at least 30 bars. This can happen several times a day. At that bar the rule checks whether price has traded at PDC at any time since today's open. If the gap is filled (a two-sided day), it FADES the break: short new highs, buy new lows. If the gap is still open (a one-sided day), it FOLLOWS the break. Entry is at the next bar's open, with target 400 and stop 500 adjusted points, under the library rules. There are 3 free parameters: 30-bar staleness, target and stop.
candidates.rationale: This is the same day-type idea as candidate 1 applied to a different trigger. It is NOT independent evidence: daily P&L correlation with candidate 1 is 0.55, and 44 of its 110 trades sit within 3 bars of a candidate-1 trade. Staleness is stable: L=20/30/45/60 bars give t 2.0-2.6 at 300/500 and 400/500, whether trading starts at the open or after 10:00. FRAGILE ALONG THE STOP AXIS: 300/500 t2.35 and 500/500 t1.5, but 400/400 t0.48, 300/400 t0.62, the diagonal 500/400 is about zero (-125), and S<=300 is about zero or negative. The edge needs the maximum 500-pt stop, which looks like a mean-reversion arm that wants room, and the best cell sits on the parameter boundary. Recent weakness: the 10-day blocks were +3953, +2002, +428, +5433, -297, +179. Lower confidence than candidate 1. It is included only so that out-of-sample can check whether the PDC day-type effect generalizes beyond the 10:00 range.

observations: Costs dominate: a random 500/500 entry loses about 30 pts, and almost every level event, in both follow and fade orientation, sits inside a t-stat band of +/-2 around random once costs are paid. What did NOT work (all tested on the 16 target/stop cells, base cost): (1) Prior-day high/low: first touch, close-break with 0 or 150-pt margin, and false-break with 5/15/30-bar windows, faded or followed: t mostly between -1.5 and +1.7. They are also rare: PDH is touched on 29% of days and PDL on 36%. (2) Prior close, prior open, prior-day midpoint and a settlement proxy (VWAP of the last 15 or 30 minutes) used as touch levels: nothing. Crossing PDC by 150 pts and following loses (t -2 to -3.8), but the fade is only t 0.3-1.7. (3) Round numbers in REAL price (grids of 250/500/1000): touch-fade at 1000 looked good (t 2.6 at 300/500), but a placebo grid shifted by 750 real points gave the same (t 2.0), and the other offsets ranged from -0.9 to +1.3. There is no round-number effect. (4) Floor pivots (P, R1, S1, R2, S2): nothing. Pivot P fade reached t 1.9 only with a wide stop. (5) Intraday swing-pivot retests (fractal N=5/10/20): both directions lose, down to t -8. (6) VWAP returns and return-to-open after an excursion: nothing. (7) Opening-range breaks: 30-minute breaks FAIL (follow t -2 to -4.9), but fading them is only t up to 2 and not stable. With no filter, 60-minute breaks are about zero in both directions. (8) Running high/low breaks after consolidation, without a filter: nothing. The 120-bar version followed reached t 2.1 with n=39. (9) ADR exhaustion (range reaching 0.8-1.2x the 5- or 10-day average): isolated cells only. (10) Gaps: fading the gap at 09:00 gives t up to 2.0, not robust. Following an UNFILLED gap with one entry at 09:15-09:24 gave t 2-3.7, but it fell to t 0.3 at 09:30, and repeated entries across a window gave t <=1.4. That was timing luck and is rejected. The gap fills on 72% of days. (11) Calendar: the discovery period holds only one WIN/IND expiry (2012-06-13) and three stock-option expiry Mondays, so calendar effects cannot be tested. Day-of-week open-to-close differences (about 12 days per weekday) are within noise. The only structure that survived is PDC used as a day-type filter, not as a price level. If the market has traded back to yesterday's close, level breaks tend to fail; if it has not, they tend to extend. It works for the 09:00-09:59 range breaks (candidate 1) and for stale-extreme breaks (candidate 2). It does NOT work for prior-day high/low breaks or 30-minute range breaks, so the support is mixed. Both candidates are clearly weaker in the last ~19 discovery days, which were also the lowest-volatility days. Process note, for transparency: my first 09:00-09:59 result (n=50, t 3.3) was partly a coding accident. My generic level-cross helper also generated crossings back INTO the range. Those inward crossings have zero edge on their own, so I rebuilt the rule with outward breaks only. Overall verdict: there is no strong level or calendar edge in this sample. Candidate 1 is a weak, plausible but unproven effect, and candidate 2 is a correlated, more fragile sibling. Given 5225 variants, a discovery t of about 3 is not convincing until it passes the locked out-of-sample test.
best_near_misses: (a) Fade-only arm of candidate 1 (09:00-09:59 range break faded on gap-filled days, outward breaks only): t 2.3-2.8 at 300/400 to 400/500, but n=37 < 40. (b) Following an unfilled gap with one entry at 09:20 (signal minute 19): n=42, t 3.2-3.7 at 500/500 and 400/500. It is fragile to the entry minute (t 0.3-0.6 at 09:30), and repeated-entry versions give t <=1.4. Rejected. (c) Round-1000 real-price touch fade at 300/500: t 2.63, n=121. A placebo grid gives the same. Rejected. (d) 30-minute range first close-break fade at 300/500: t 1.96, n=146, halves balanced, but not stable across targets. (e) Running high/low break after 120 bars of consolidation, followed, at 400/500: t 2.1, n=39. (f) ADR5 exhaustion fade at k=0.8, 200/400: t 2.37, n=38, isolated cell.

candidates.name: ml_wf_open_fade_lr
candidates.description: This is a fade back toward the day's open in the first 90 minutes of the session, picked by a walk-forward logistic model. On each 1-minute bar from 09:00 to 10:29 it computes r = log(close / first open of the day) in bp. A frozen logistic regression that treats long and short symmetrically scores P(win) for a long (feature +r) and for a short (feature -r). It trades when P(win) is above the 80th percentile of the training predictions. In practice: when price is more than about 32 bp above the day's open it sells, and when it is more than about 32 bp below it buys. Entry is at the next bar's open with target 400 / stop 400, one position at a time, forced exit at end of day. It uses only the close, open, day and mod columns, implements inference in pure numpy and passes lookahead_check.
candidates.rationale: These are WALK-FORWARD OUT-OF-SAMPLE stats. The model is retrained every 5 days on an expanding window, trained on days before each block and tested on discovery days 20-58 (39 days). The threshold is the training-set 80% quantile. Economic story: moves in the futures-led early session (before the US cash open at 10:30 BRT) tend to overshoot and pull back toward the open. Supporting evidence: in the 09:00-10:30 window, the daily rank correlation (IC) between the model score and trade outcome is 0.27-0.43 out of sample, with t = 5 to 8, across 5 target/stop pairs. Neighbours also pass. 36 of 108 walk-forward neighbours pass every bar test: windows ending at 80, 90 or 100 minutes, threshold quantiles 0.75 and 0.80, and target/stop from 300 to 500. Retraining every 1 or 10 days instead of every 5 also passes (t 2.3-2.5). Caveats you must weigh: (1) I chose the window and the feature after seeing out-of-sample ICs from the same days 20-58, so these walk-forward numbers are biased upward by that selection. (2) The edge is concentrated in time. Days 0-19 (May 2012, a downtrend) show NO edge: the frozen rule makes -859 pts on those days, and a walk-forward version trading from day 10 loses on days 10-19. Days 20-39 carry most of the profit (+130 pts/trade), and days 40-58 are only modestly positive (+30-70 pts/trade, not significant on their own). (3) Frozen in-sample on all 59 days the rule gives t_daily = 1.95 at 400/400 (2.2 at 500/500 and 500/400), which is weaker than the walk-forward number. (4) A higher threshold (q = 0.85, which needs bigger moves) is weak, with t of only 0.4-1.1. That suggests big early moves continue (trend days) and only moderate ones revert, so the edge depends on the regime. (5) I tested 1552 variants in total. Treat this as a marginal, regime-dependent candidate that needs the locked validation.

observations:
GENERIC ML ON 1-MINUTE FEATURES FOUND NOTHING. I tried logistic regression, ridge, depth-3 trees, and shallow gradient boosting (classifier and regressor) on 51 causal features: returns over 1-120 bars, volatility, volume and time-of-day volume, distance to VWAP and to the session high/low, previous-day levels, gap, signed flow, and trend efficiency. Labels were bracket profit and loss from outcomes() for long and short, plus forward 10/30/60-minute returns. All of it was walk-forward with an expanding window from day 20 and retraining every 5 days. Out-of-sample daily IC was about 0 (|t| < 1 in almost every case), and the top decile earned only about +10-20 pts/trade, against roughly -30 for random entries. Nothing came close to t >= 2 with n >= 40.

SEPARATE LONG AND SHORT MODELS WERE WORSE THAN RANDOM. Fitted separately, the linear models lost -40 to -90 pts/trade out of sample. They learned the period's down drift and day-level effects that later reversed.

POOLING LONG AND SHORT REMOVES THE DRIFT. Training one model on long and short samples together, with every signed feature flipped for the short side, removes that drift bias and brings these models back to about -0 to -10 pts/trade. I recommend this as standard practice.

STRATEGIES THAT WORKED RECENTLY TEND TO FLIP. The daily IC of momentum-type features has negative persistence across days (correlation of -0.2 to -0.27 with the trailing 5-day IC). This explains why naively retrained models flip sign. It is too weak (t of about 2, with many tests) to trade on.

THE ONLY ROBUST STRUCTURE IS IN THE OPENING SESSION (09:00-10:30 BRT). Within that window, return since the day's open (r_day) is strongly contrarian: fading the move beats following it on most days, in both halves (daily IC t of -4.5 and -3.6). Its frequent-trading version is my one candidate. Within the window, entries in 09:00-09:15 lose and the profit comes from entries at 09:30-10:30. Extending the window to 11:00 or later kills the effect, because after the US cash open at 10:30 BRT early moves tend to continue. The effect barely exists in May 2012 (days 0-19, a downtrend with higher volatility) and is strongest in June.

THE GAP POINTS THE SAME WAY BUT ADDS LITTLE. The overnight gap is mildly continuation-like (daily IC t of about 2). Fading a move that extends the gap loses, while fading a move that fills the gap wins in all three thirds of the period. Adding the gap to the model raised IC (0.43) but did NOT improve trading results (t 1.4-1.8). I did not submit it.

EVENT STUDIES. Fading the first break of the opening range (15 or 30 minutes) had positive average profit in both halves, but a full target/stop grid on all discovery days peaked at t of about 2.2, and only with target 200 / stop 500. Breakouts of the session high/low, VWAP crosses and big-bar continuation or fade had no edge.

COSTS AND HOLDING TIMES. 200/200 brackets are hopeless after costs (about 32 pts per round trip; median hold of 4 minutes). Median hold is about 27 minutes for 500/500. Long and short outcomes are nearly symmetric, about -30 pts/trade for random entries.

HONESTY NOTES. I made 1552 evaluations in total (logged). Choosing the opening window and the r_day feature used out-of-sample days 20-58, so the walk-forward stats are optimistic. In-sample on all 59 days the frozen candidate has t = 1.95 at 400/400. My expectation for the locked validation is a coin flip at best.
best_near_misses: (a) The same opening model with return since open plus gap: walk-forward t 1.81 at 400/400, q = 0.8, n = 111, both halves positive. IC is higher but it did not pass t >= 2. (b) Shallow gradient boosting on all features, 400/400, q = 0.98: t 2.27 but n = 36 < 40, and it is an isolated spike. (c) Fading the first break of the opening range (15 or 30 minutes), target 200 / stop 500: full-discovery t of about 2.2-2.24 after a scan of 96 parameter sets. The win rate is high (81%) but the payoff is lopsided (small wins, big losses), and the result is not robust to the target. (d) The opening fade at 500/500 under walk-forward: t 2.08, n = 89, second half only +430. It is the same rule as the candidate, so not submitted separately.
